title: SLO Commitment Negotiation and Delegation Playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook defines a repeatable process for negotiating SLO commitments with product teams, delegating SLO stewardship, and converting commitments into capacity reservations and error-budget guardrails. It emphasizes pragmatic tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs availability) and formal handoffs to ensure measurable accountability.

Goals
- Produce SLO agreements that are measurable, testable, and pair with concrete capacity commitments.
- Reduce negotiation friction and speed up safe rollouts.
- Ensure error-budget actions and capacity changes are enacted automatically where possible, or with clear human approval steps.

Scope
Applies to: model-serving services, inference frontends, embedding pipelines, and any tenant-facing inference subsystem. Excludes internal-only batch analytics (handled by infra-cost team).

Definitions
- SLI: Service Level Indicator (e.g., p99 latency excluding cold starts; 99.9% inference success).
- SLO: Service Level Objective (target value for an SLI over a rolling window).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO over the evaluation window (commonly 28 days).
- Steward: individual responsible for SLO health, runbook updates, and coordination.

SLO Taxonomy and Examples
Use this taxonomy when negotiating:
- Latency SLOs (user-facing): p50/p95/p99 tail per route, measured at ingress after auth.
- Availability SLOs (success rate): 5xx+4xx-excluding-rate-limited / total requests.
- Correctness SLOs (quality): task-specific metric, e.g., regression against verified prompt set (for core models).
- Cost-awareness indicators: tokens-per-request and mean GPU-ms per request (inform capacity reservations).

Example baseline commitments (starting point for negotiations):
- Hosted-generation-default: p95 <= 350ms, success >= 99.5% (28d), error budget 0.5%.
- Large-context-chat: p95 <= 800ms, success >= 99.0% (28d), error budget 1.0%.
- Embeddings-batch: p95 <= 1200ms, success >= 99.8% (28d), error budget 0.2%.
(These are examples — negotiate per-tenant when needed.)

Negotiation Process (Step-by-step)
1) Preparation (Product Owner + SRE Steward)
   - Gather: expected QPS, request size distribution (tokens), critical routes, SLA requirements, geographic constraints.
   - Run the capacity estimator tool (see Appendix) with 14-day traffic forecast.
   - Prepare a recommended SLO and a conservative capacity reservation (GPU hours + burst allowance).
2) First-pass negotiation (cross-functional meeting)
   - Present tradeoffs: lower latency requires higher reserved capacity or higher cost. Show cost delta estimates.
   - Propose two-tier options: Standard (lower cost, higher error budget) and Premium (lower latency, dedicated capacity).
   - Capture non-functional constraints: data residency, private deployment needs.
3) Draft SLO contract (SRE drafts)
   - SLO statement (metric, window, target), monitoring sources, alerting thresholds, runbook reference, steward assignment, capacity reservation ID.
   - Attach rollback and phased rollout plan (canary percentages and step durations).
4) Sign-off and storage
   - Product PO and SRE steward sign off in the confluence contract page. The contract is versioned and stored under the product’s folder.
5) Implementation
   - Create capacity reservation ticket in Capacity Tracking board with exact machine types, commit windows, and autoscale policies.
   - Wire alerts and dashboards (see Telemetry section).
6) Operationalization
   - Configure error-budget controller thresholds (auto-throttle at 50% consumed, escalation window at 75%).
   - Schedule monthly review in SLO standing meeting.

Delegation and Stewardship Matrix
- Product Owner: defines feature-level criticality and approves SLO tradeoffs.
- SRE Steward: owns SLO definition, alerting, runbook updates, and capacity negotiations.
- Platform Capacity Manager: implements reservation, cost tracking, and shares forecasting.
- Oncall (Service): executes runbook steps and coordinates incident escalation.

Capacity Commitment Flow (mapping SLO -> resources)
1) Telemetry-derived baseline (7d): compute mean and 95th token lengths, QPS distribution per route.
2) Model profile lookup: tokens-to-GPU-ms conversion from benchmarking matrix.
3) Safety margin: apply 30% headroom default (tunable per tenant).
4) Reservation plan: CPU/GPU count, node types, local NVMe needs, and network egress estimate.
5) Autoscale policy: minimum reserved fraction and burstable ceiling with graceful fallbacks to smaller models.

Capacity Negotiation Template (summary for execs)
- Proposed SLO: p95 latency <= 350ms, success >= 99.5% (28d)
- Expected steady QPS: 120
- Mean tokens per request: 180
- Profiled GPU-ms/request: 42ms (A100-40GB equivalent)
- Reserve: 6 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equiv) + 30% headroom
- Estimated monthly cost delta: $XXk
- Action: approve reservation or accept Standard tier with p95 <= 550ms and shared capacity

Telemetry and Evidence (what to wire)
- Essential SLIs: ingress_p95_latency_ms, request_success_rate, tokens_per_request, gpu_ms_per_request
- Dashboards: 28d rolling SLO summary, per-route latency heatmap, error-budget burn-down chart.
- Alerts:
  - SLO-warning: error_budget_remaining < 50% over 24h -> Pager (severity: low) to SRE steward
  - SLO-escalation: error_budget_remaining < 25% over 6h -> Pager (severity: high) + product PO notification
  - Immediate-degradation: request_success_rate drops below target - 0.5% absolute -> Pager to oncall (severity: critical)
- Evidence collection: link to saved traces, a slice example (tenant, route, time range), and pre-populated playback queries.

Runbook: SLO Depletion and Mitigation Procedure
1) Triage (oncall)
   - Verify telemetry: confirm SLI alert, check burn rate, and scope (tenant vs global).
   - Execute quick containment: throttle non-critical routes, divert to cached responses, or reduce model context length.
2) Temporary capacity actions
   - If autoscale available: increase replica count up to the burst ceiling.
   - If reservation needed: request pre-approved burst tokens (see Capacity board fast-path).
3) Degradation plan (when capacity cannot be added)
   - Apply graceful degradation policy: route lower-priority tenants to lower-cost model variant; enable token cap per request.
4) Communication
   - Post to status page with clear user-facing impact, ETA, and mitigation actions.
   - Notify sales/customer-success for affected enterprise customers.
5) Post-incident
   - Create incident ticket, collect slices and artifacts, and run the incident-review checklist (see Incident Review Standards).

Incident Review Standards (brief)
- Trigger: any event that consumes >50% of error budget in 24h or any P0 outage.
- Required deliverables: timeline, evidence, root cause hypothesis, mitigation record, and remediation plan with owners and deadlines.
- Blameless facilitation: SRE steward runs the review within 5 business days.

Operational Tooling Recommendations
- Capacity estimator: runcapacity --service <name> --window 14d --safety 0.3 (returns GPU-hours + suggested node types).
- Error-budget controller: configure with the following thresholds in the orchestration UI: warning=0.5, escalate=0.25, hard-stop=0.05.
- Dashboard snippets (Grafana/Panel IDs included as text): panel ids: latency-overview-034, errorbudget-burn-121, per-route-heat-507.

Rollout and Canary Guidelines
- Canary cadence: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% with at least 30 minutes at each stage and SLO checks.
- Abort criteria: any canary stage that increases error burn rate by >3x baseline or produces >0.5% absolute drop in success rate.

Templates & Examples
- Contract excerpt:
  SLO: ingress_p95_latency_ms <= 350ms (28d); Measurement point: ingress-proxy v2; Steward: <name>
  Capacity reservation: reservation-2025-ACCT-42; Node type: a100-40gb; Min replicas: 3; Burst ceiling: 9

- Example alert query (PromQL-like pseudocode):
  1 - (sum(successful_requests) by (service) / sum(total_requests) by (service))
  Use rolling_window = 28d and compare to contract target.

Appendix: Practical checks before sign-off
- Confirm telemetry sources (traces, metrics, logs) are producing for the full retention period.
- Run synthetic canary to validate p95 under a 1.5x expected load.
- Confirm policy for emergency preemptive scaling and customer communication.

Ownership and maintenance
- SRE stewards must review active SLOs quarterly, and trigger a negotiation if traffic patterns shift >25% or if cost exceeds projections by >15%.
- Archive retired SLO contracts after 2 years; keep a read-only audit trail.

Contact points
- Oncall rotations: see /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-and-incident-response
- Capacity board: #capacity-tracking (internal)

Revision history
